unit.title: Perform thermal straightening, curling and waving

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: How long does a thermal press (with a pressing comb or flat iron) usually last?
options: For ever, like a relaxer
Until the hair grows out of the scalp
For exactly one year
Until the hair gets wet or very damp

questions.stem: Why does pressed hair 'go back' (revert) in hot, humid weather?
options: Moisture in the air lets it return to its natural shape
The hot sun burns the straight hair back into tight curls
Humidity makes the client's hair grow out much faster
Heat from the sun sets the pressing oil hard on the hair

questions.stem: How is thermal straightening different from a chemical relaxer?
options: Thermal straightening is permanent; a relaxer washes out at once
Thermal straightening is temporary; a relaxer is permanent
Both are permanent and both need a neutralising shampoo
Both use the very same chemicals, but one uses heat

questions.stem: What condition should the hair be in before pressing or flat ironing?
options: Damp, so the heat does not burn it
Dirty, so the natural oils protect it
Clean and completely dry
Coated with a thick setting gel

questions.stem: Why must the hair be completely dry before a hot iron touches it?
options: Damp hair makes the hot iron cool down far too fast
Water turns to steam, which can burn the hair
Only dry hair can hold the pressing oil on it properly
Damp hair will not take in any of the heat protectant

questions.stem: How is natural coily hair usually prepared to make pressing easier and gentler?
options: Brushed hard while it is dry to loosen the coils
Set on small perm rods while it is wet
Blow-dried with a comb nozzle to stretch it
Left in very tight braids overnight first

questions.stem: Why is a heat protectant applied before using thermal tools?
options: To make the hair curl up much tighter
To help shield the hair from heat damage
To make the iron heat up much faster
To add a little colour while the hair is styled

questions.stem: How should you test the heat of a pressing comb before it touches the hair?
options: Touch the teeth quickly with the tip of your finger
Test it on a white tissue or towel for scorching
Hold it near the client's cheek to feel how hot it is
Run it through your own hair first to see if it smokes

questions.stem: When you test a pressing comb, the tissue turns brown. What should you do?
options: Let the comb cool, then test it again
Use it at once, because it is now ready
Dip it in water to cool it fast
Add more pressing oil to the hair

questions.stem: Why is a comb placed between a hot curling iron and the scalp?
options: To hold the curl in place while it cools
To make the iron hotter near the root
To protect the scalp from burns
To part the hair for the next curl

questions.stem: How should the client's ear be protected when you press or curl hair near it?
options: Ask the client to hold a wet towel over the ear
Put pressing oil on the ear first
Work very fast so that the heat does not reach it
Hold the ear down and keep the tool away from it

questions.stem: Which part of a pressing comb does most of the straightening?
options: The very tips of the teeth
The wooden handle at the end
The heater it sits in
The back (spine) of the comb

questions.stem: Why do many pressing combs have a wooden handle?
options: Wood makes the metal comb heat up faster
Wood makes the comb much lighter to carry
Wood does not get hot, so it is safe to hold
Wood keeps the metal teeth perfectly straight

questions.stem: What is a 'soft press'?
options: Pressing each side of the section twice with very high heat
Pressing each side of the section once with light pressure
Pressing only the ends, never the roots
Pressing the hair while it is still damp

questions.stem: Why should a hard (double) press not be done often?
options: It makes the hair revert much faster in the rain
It uses too much pressing oil
It takes the curl out only at the ends
The extra heat can damage and break the hair

questions.stem: Why are small sections used when pressing natural hair?
options: Small sections let you use more pressing oil
Large sections make the pressing comb far too hot
The heat can pass evenly through each section
Small sections make the hair revert slowly

questions.stem: Why should only a small amount of pressing oil or cream be used?
options: Oil makes the hot comb cool down far too quickly
Too little oil makes the hair revert
Pressing oil is too costly to use on every section
Too much can smoke and weigh the hair down

questions.stem: Which hair usually needs the lowest heat setting on a flat iron?
options: Coarse, thick natural hair
Healthy, dense hair that is hard to straighten
Fine, damaged or chemically treated hair
Hair that has not been pressed before

questions.stem: When using a flat iron, why is it better to make a few smooth passes than many quick ones?
options: Repeated passes add heat damage to the same hair
Fewer passes help the iron heat back up much faster
Many passes make the hair curl up
Fewer passes use less heat protectant

questions.stem: What is the 'comb chase' method with a flat iron?
options: Combing the hair back after the iron to add curl
Combing the hair after it has cooled for an hour
Combing just ahead of the iron as it glides down
Using two irons at once on the same section

questions.stem: What is a Marcel wave?
options: A wet set made with the fingers and gel
A perm wave made with chemicals and rods
An S-shaped wave made with a hot Marcel iron
A braid that makes the hair wavy when undone

questions.stem: What are the two main parts of a curling (Marcel) iron that hold the hair?
options: The rod and the shell (groove)
The teeth and the back (spine)
The two flat plates and the hinge
The nozzle and the diffuser head

questions.stem: What is a croquignole curl?
options: A curl wound from the scalp to the ends along the iron
A curl wound from the ends up towards the scalp
A flat curl pinned with a clip
A curl made without heat

questions.stem: Why should a curl be left to cool before it is combed out?
options: The curl sets as it cools, so it lasts longer
Combing warm hair makes the curl much tighter
Combing warm hair can melt the plastic comb
Combing warm hair stops the heat protectant working

questions.stem: Before using an electric flat iron, what should you check?
options: That the cord and plug are not damaged and the plates are clean
That the iron is plugged into a socket next to the shampoo basin
That the cord is wrapped tightly round the iron to keep it tidy
That the iron is at its highest heat for every client

questions.stem: Where should a hot iron be put down between uses?
options: On the client's lap, resting on a folded towel
On the edge of the basin
In a heat-resistant holder or on a heat mat
On top of the trolley's paper towels

questions.stem: What should you do with thermal tools at the end of the service?
options: Leave them switched on for the next client
Put them straight into a closed drawer while still hot
Switch off, unplug and let them cool safely
Cool them quickly under the tap

questions.stem: Before using a new electric hot tool, what should you check on its label?
options: That it is the same colour as the other tools
That it weighs less than one kilogram
That it was made in the last month
That it suits the Centre's supply voltage

questions.stem: A client's ear is burnt by a hot comb. What should you do first?
options: Put butter or oil on the burn
Rub ice straight onto the burn
Cover it with hair gel to cool it
Cool it under cool running water

questions.stem: For about how long should a minor burn be cooled under cool running water?
options: About 20 minutes
About 10 seconds
About 1 minute
About 2 hours

questions.stem: Which scalp condition means you should not do a thermal service today?
options: A healthy scalp with a few grey hairs
Hair that is tangled after washing
Hair that is coarse and dense
Cuts or sores on the scalp

questions.stem: Why should you use less heat on relaxed or coloured hair?
options: Relaxed hair cannot get hot because it is straight
It is weaker, so it burns or breaks more easily
Coloured hair can turn green when heat touches it
Relaxed hair is straight, so it needs no heat at all

questions.stem: Which sign shows that natural hair may have heat damage?
options: The hair feels soft and looks healthy and shiny
The curl no longer comes back after washing
The hair reverts to curls in humid weather
The ends curl up again after shampooing

questions.stem: During pressing you smell burning hair. What should you do?
options: Stop, check the heat and lower it before going on
Carry on, because a smell of burning hair is normal
Add more pressing oil to the section and go on
Press much faster so that the smell goes away

questions.stem: How should a pressing comb be cleaned?
options: Dip it into cold water while it is still very hot
Scrape it with a knife while it is still in the heater
Wipe off build-up when cool, as the maker says
Never clean it, because the old oil protects the metal

questions.stem: How should the plates of a flat iron be cleaned between clients?
options: Wiped when cool, then disinfected as the maker says
Scrubbed hard with steel wool while still hot
Rinsed under the tap while it is still plugged in
Left with old product on them to protect the plates

questions.stem: Why should the thermal styling area be well ventilated?
options: To keep the iron at a steady heat all the time
To dry the client's hair faster
To make the curls set more quickly
To clear smoke and fumes from heated products

questions.stem: What advice helps pressed hair stay straight for longer?
options: Wrap it at night and keep it away from moisture
Wash it every morning to keep it fresh and clean
Spray it with water each morning to add shine
Go to the gym and swim without covering the hair

questions.stem: Why should a client not have her hair pressed every few days?
options: It makes the client's hair grow far too fast
Pressing works only once a month
It makes the scalp too oily
Frequent high heat can cause lasting damage

questions.stem: Why should the edges (the hair along the front hairline) be pressed with less heat?
options: The edges grow back much faster than other hair
Hairline hair is often finer and burns easily
The edges never revert, so need no heat at all
Pressing oil does not work at all on the edges

questions.stem: How do you check that a press is finished?
options: The hair smokes a little when the comb touches it
The hair feels stiff and well coated in oil all over
Each section is smooth from root to end
The client's scalp feels warm to the touch all over

questions.stem: Besides straightening, what else can a flat iron be used for?
options: Drying wet hair quickly before a set
Making curls by turning it as it glides
Cutting split ends off the hair with heat
Mixing colour on the hair

questions.stem: Why do you ask a client how often she uses heat on her hair at home?
options: To judge the risk of heat damage
To sell her a brand new flat iron from the salon
To decide whether she also needs a short haircut
So that you can charge her more for the service

questions.stem: How should the cords of thermal tools be kept during a service?
options: Stretched right across the walkway to the chair
Tidy and clear of the floor, away from water
Wrapped round the client's chair
Hanging in the shampoo basin

questions.stem: A flat iron sparks when you switch it on. What should you do?
options: Tap it on the trolley to fix it
Carry on if it still heats up
Wrap tape round the cord and carry on using it
Unplug it, label it faulty and report it

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: Which bonds in the hair are broken by heat and water, so that the hair can change shape for a while?
What word describes pressed hair going back to its natural curl when it gets damp?
What type of press uses one pass on each side of the section, with a little more pressure than a soft press?
What is the name of the device that a pressing comb is heated in?
Pressing combs are usually made of brass or of which other metal?
What does the dial or thermostat on an electric flat iron control?
What curl is made by winding the hair along the length of the iron, like a corkscrew?
What are the rollers called that are heated in a unit and used to set dry hair in curls?
Name a smooth fabric for a scarf or pillowcase that helps keep pressed hair smooth at night.
Which comb, with a long thin handle, is used to make neat partings for thermal sections?
What is the name of the burn caused by hot steam, for example when a hot iron touches wet hair?
What word describes how many hairs there are on the head, for example thin or thick?
Where must an accident, such as a burn to a client, be written down?
What name is given to a thermal service on natural hair that uses a blow-dryer and then a flat iron to give very smooth, shiny hair?
What do we call hair ends that have split into two or more strands?

essays.stem: Explain how heat straightens or curls the hair, and why the result is only temporary.
essays.modelAnswer: Hair has many small links inside it called hydrogen bonds. They help to hold the hair in its natural shape, and they are broken by water and by heat. When a hot pressing comb, flat iron or curling iron is drawn through dry hair, the heat breaks many of these hydrogen bonds and lets the hair take a new shape, straight or curled. As the hair cools in its new shape, the bonds re-form and hold it there for a while. The strong disulphide bonds are not changed by heat styling, so the natural curl is still there. When the hair gets wet, or takes in moisture from humid air or sweat, the hydrogen bonds break again and the hair returns to its natural shape. This is called reversion. That is why a press lasts only until the next shampoo or until the hair gets damp, unlike a relaxer, which is permanent.
markingPoints: Hydrogen bonds hold the shape and are broken by water and heat
Heat breaks them so the hair takes a new shape
The bonds re-form as the hair cools, holding the shape for a while
Disulphide bonds are not changed, so the natural curl remains
Moisture or humidity makes the hair revert, so the result is temporary

essays.stem: Describe what you would ask and check during a consultation before a thermal straightening or curling service.
essays.modelAnswer: I ask the client what result she wants, such as a soft press, a silk press or curls, and how long she wants it to last. I ask about chemical services, such as relaxers or colour, and when they were done, because treated hair needs less heat. I ask how often she uses heat at home, and whether she has had heat damage or a burn before. I look at her scalp for cuts, sores, burns or signs of infection; if I find any, I do not do the service and advise her to see a doctor. I check the hair's texture, density, porosity, elasticity and condition, and look for breakage, split ends and areas that no longer curl. I check the fine hair at the edges. From this I choose the tools, the heat setting and the products. I explain the result and the aftercare, agree the price and time, and fill in the record card.
markingPoints: Agrees the result wanted
Asks about chemical services and heat use at home
Checks the scalp and does not proceed (refers) if there are cuts, sores or infection
Checks texture, density, porosity, elasticity, condition and the edges
Chooses tools, heat and products to suit; agrees and records

essays.stem: Describe how you would prepare natural coily hair for a press, from shampoo to sectioning.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check the scalp is healthy. I shampoo the hair gently to remove oil, dirt and product build-up, because product left on the hair can burn and smoke. I apply a moisturising conditioner and detangle the hair in sections with my fingers and a wide-tooth comb, working from the ends up to the roots. I rinse, then blot the hair with a towel. I apply a heat protectant to the damp hair, as the maker says. Then I blow-dry the hair in sections with a comb nozzle on a medium heat, to stretch it and get it completely dry, because damp hair will steam and burn under a hot comb. When the hair is fully dry, I divide it into four main sections with a tail comb and clip them. I then work in small sub-sections, so that the heat can pass evenly through each one.
markingPoints: Checks the scalp, then shampoos to remove build-up
Conditions and detangles from the ends up
Applies heat protectant as the maker says
Blow-dries with a comb nozzle to stretch the hair until completely dry
Sections into four and works in small sub-sections

essays.stem: Describe the steps for pressing a section of natural hair with a pressing comb, safely and correctly.
essays.modelAnswer: With the hair clean, completely dry and protected, I heat the pressing comb in its heater. Before it touches the hair, I test it on a white tissue or towel. If the tissue scorches or turns brown, the comb is too hot, so I let it cool and test it again. I wipe the comb clean. I take a small section and comb it smooth, and add a very small amount of pressing oil or cream if needed. I hold the section out from the head, away from the scalp. I put the teeth of the comb into the top of the section near the root, but not touching the scalp, then turn the comb so that the back (spine) presses the hair, and draw it slowly to the ends. For a soft press, I do this once on each side. I protect the ear by holding it down, and I use less heat on the fine hair at the edges.
markingPoints: Hair clean, completely dry, with heat protectant
Tests the comb on a white tissue or towel, and lets it cool if it scorches
Takes a small section, holds it away from the scalp, uses only a little oil
Inserts the teeth near the root and draws through with the back of the comb
Protects the ears and scalp; uses less heat on the edges

essays.stem: Describe how you would give a silk press with a flat iron, and how you keep the hair and the client safe.
essays.modelAnswer: I shampoo and deep-condition the hair, detangle it gently, and apply a heat protectant. I blow-dry it in sections with a comb nozzle until it is stretched and completely dry. I check the flat iron's cord and plug and make sure the plates are clean. I set the heat to suit the hair: lower for fine, damaged or treated hair. I test the iron on a tissue or towel first. I divide the hair into four sections, then take small sub-sections. I comb each sub-section smooth and use the comb chase method, combing just ahead of the iron as it glides slowly from the root to the ends, keeping the plates away from the scalp and ears. I make as few passes as I need. I rest the iron on a heat mat between sections and keep the cord tidy. At the end I check the hair is smooth from root to end, switch off, unplug and leave the iron to cool.
markingPoints: Shampoos, conditions, detangles, applies heat protectant and blow-dries until dry
Checks the iron and sets heat to suit the hair; tests on a tissue or towel
Small sub-sections with the comb chase method, root to ends
Keeps plates away from the scalp and ears; few passes
Rests the iron safely, checks the result, then switches off, unplugs and cools

essays.stem: Describe how to make thermal curls with a curling iron, and how you protect the scalp and ears.
essays.modelAnswer: The hair must be clean, dry and protected with a heat protectant. I check the iron and its cord, set a heat that suits the hair, and test it on a white tissue or towel first. I take a small section, no wider than the iron, and comb it smooth. I hold the section out from the head at the angle I need for the volume I want. I open the iron, place it on the hair near the ends, and close it. For a croquignole curl, I wind the hair from the ends up towards the scalp, turning the iron and opening and closing it slightly so the hair moves smoothly. I stop before I reach the scalp and place a comb between the iron and the scalp to protect it. I hold the client's ear down and away. I hold the iron for a few seconds, then slide it out gently and let the curl cool, pinned if needed, before combing it out.
markingPoints: Hair clean, dry and protected; iron checked and tested on a tissue or towel
Small, smooth sections held at the right angle
Winds the curl correctly (for example from the ends to the scalp)
Places a comb between the iron and the scalp and protects the ears
Releases the curl gently and lets it cool before combing

essays.stem: Explain how you would use electric thermal tools and a pressing comb heater safely in the salon.
essays.modelAnswer: Before I use a tool, I check that the cord, plug and casing are not damaged and that the tool suits the Centre's supply voltage. If anything is damaged or sparks, I do not use it; I unplug it, label it faulty and report it. I plug tools into a proper socket away from the basin and water, and I keep my hands dry. I keep the cords tidy and off the floor, so nobody trips, and never wrap a cord round a hot tool. I rest hot tools in a heat-resistant holder or on a heat mat, never on towels, paper or the client. I keep the pressing comb heater away from anything that can burn, and I do not leave a hot tool alone. I keep the area ventilated to clear smoke from products. At the end, I switch off, unplug, and let the tools cool in a safe place before cleaning and storing them.
markingPoints: Checks cords, plugs and the voltage label before use
Does not use damaged tools: unplugs, labels and reports them
Keeps tools and sockets away from water; dry hands; tidy cords
Rests hot tools in a holder or on a heat mat; keeps the heater away from flammables; never leaves them alone
Switches off, unplugs and cools before cleaning and storing

essays.stem: Describe the signs of heat damage in hair, its causes, and how you can prevent it.
essays.modelAnswer: Heat-damaged hair often feels dry and rough and looks dull. It may have split ends and break easily. On natural hair, a common sign is that the curl does not come back after washing, so some parts stay straight or limp. Burnt hair may smell, look scorched or change colour. The causes include heat that is too high for the hair, many passes over the same section, pressing hair that is damp, using too much oil, pressing too often, and not using a heat protectant. Chemically treated, fine or damaged hair and the edges are most at risk. To prevent it, I check the hair during the consultation, choose a heat that suits the hair, and test the tool on a tissue or towel. I always use a heat protectant on clean, dry hair, work in small sections with few passes, and stop at once if I smell burning. I advise the client not to use heat too often.
markingPoints: Signs: dry, rough, dull hair, split ends and breakage
Natural hair that no longer curls back after washing; burnt smell or scorching
Causes: too much heat, many passes, damp hair, too much oil, too often, no protectant
Prevention: suitable heat, test on tissue or towel, heat protectant on dry hair
Small sections, few passes, stop if burning; advise less frequent heat

essays.stem: Describe what you would do if a client is burnt on the scalp or ear during a thermal service.
essays.modelAnswer: I stop the service at once, put the hot tool down safely in its holder, and switch it off. I stay calm and reassure the client. I cool the burn under cool running water for about 20 minutes, or with a clean cloth soaked in cool water if it is on the scalp and running water is hard to use. I do not put ice, butter, oil, toothpaste or hair products on it, and I do not break any blisters. After cooling, I cover it loosely with a clean, non-fluffy dressing if it needs covering. I call the instructor or the Centre's first aider. If the burn is large, deep, blistered or on the face, the client must get medical help. I write what happened in the accident book. Afterwards, I check what caused it, such as a tool that was too hot or a missing comb guard, so that it does not happen again.
markingPoints: Stops, puts the tool down safely and switches it off
Cools the burn with cool running water for about 20 minutes
Does not use ice, butter, oil or products; does not break blisters
Covers it loosely, gets the first aider, and gets medical help if serious
Records it in the accident book and finds the cause

essays.stem: What aftercare advice would you give after a press, and how would you clean and store the thermal tools?
essays.modelAnswer: I would advise the client to keep her hair away from moisture, rain, steam and sweat, because water will make it revert. She can wrap her hair at night and cover it with a satin or silk scarf or bonnet. She should use light, non-water-based products sparingly, and comb it gently. She should not press or flat iron it again every few days, and should always use a heat protectant and low heat at home. Regular deep conditioning and trims keep the hair healthy. To clean the tools, I first switch them off, unplug them and let them cool. I wipe the flat iron and curling iron plates with a damp cloth, then disinfect them as the maker says. I remove oil and carbon build-up from the pressing comb when it is cool, as the maker says. I wash and disinfect combs and clips. I store the tools dry, with the cords loosely coiled, in a safe place.
markingPoints: Keep hair away from moisture and sweat; wrap at night with a satin or silk scarf
Light products; do not use heat again too often; use protectant and low heat at home
Deep conditioning and trims
Switches off, unplugs and cools tools before cleaning
Wipes and disinfects plates as the maker says; cleans the comb when cool; stores dry with cords loosely coiled

practical1.title: Soft press with a pressing comb on natural hair, finished with thermal curls
practical1.brief: As a group, give a soft press to natural coily hair on a model who agrees to it, or on a practice head with textured human hair, and finish it with thermal curls. Share the work: one member leads the consultation, checks the scalp and fills in the record card; one shampoos, conditions and detangles the hair; one applies heat protectant and blow-dries it with a comb nozzle until it is completely dry; one sets up and checks the heater and pressing comb. Then the hair is divided into four sections and each member presses at least one section while the assessor watches. Before each use, the member tests the comb on a white tissue or towel and shows the result, then protects the scalp and the ears. Last, each member makes at least two curls with a curling iron, with a comb between the iron and the scalp. Photograph each stage below, showing the hair only, never the face unless the model agrees and the Centre allows it. Switch off, unplug and cool all tools, clean up, and hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A model who agrees, or a practice head with natural textured human hair
Curling iron with a stand or heat mat
Heat protectant and a small amount of pressing oil or cream
White tissues or paper towels for heat testing
Shampoo, conditioner, towels, capes and neck strips
Wide-tooth comb, tail comb, hard rubber comb and clips
Satin scarf for the finished style
photos: The station set up, with tools checked and heat mat in place
The hair blow-dried and divided into four sections
A heat test on a white tissue or towel
A section being pressed, with the ear held away
The pressed hair, smooth from root to end
The finished curls, with a comb guard shown during curling
The tools switched off, unplugged and cooling, and the area clean
checklist: Checked the scalp and hair before starting
Made sure the hair was clean and completely dry, with heat protectant on
Tested the pressing comb on a white tissue or towel before each use
Pressed small sections evenly from root to end without touching the scalp
Protected the ears and edges and used little oil
Made thermal curls with a comb between the iron and the scalp
Rested hot tools safely and kept cords tidy
Switched off, unplugged and cooled the tools, then cleaned the area
safety: Test every hot tool on a white tissue or towel before it touches the hair
Protect the scalp and ears; never press damp hair
Rest hot tools only in a holder or on a heat mat; keep cords off the floor and away from water
Cool any burn under cool running water for about 20 minutes and tell the instructor
Keep the area ventilated and the heater away from anything that can burn

practical2.title: Silk press with a flat iron, with curls and waves made with irons
practical2.brief: As a group, give a silk press with a flat iron and then style it with curls and waves, on a model who agrees to it or on practice heads with natural or relaxed human hair. Share the work: one member leads the consultation and chooses the heat setting with the group, writing the reason on the record card; one shampoos, conditions and detangles the hair; one applies heat protectant and blow-dries it until completely dry. Each member then flat irons at least one section with the comb chase method, keeping the plates away from the scalp and ears. Next, each member styles one area: spiral curls, croquignole curls, or waves made with a curling iron or flat iron. Every member tests the tool on a tissue or towel before use and rests it on a heat mat between sections. Photograph each stage below, showing the hair only, never the face unless the model agrees and the Centre allows it. Switch off, unplug and cool all tools, clean the plates as the maker says, and hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A model who agrees, or practice heads with natural or relaxed human hair
Flat iron with a heat control, and a curling iron
White tissues or paper towels for heat testing
Shampoo, conditioner, towels, capes and neck strips
Wide-tooth comb, tail comb, fine comb and clips
Disinfectant wipes or spray for the plates, as the maker says
photos: The tools checked, with cords tidy and heat mats in place
The record card showing the heat setting chosen and why
The comb chase method on one section
The finished silk press from the back
The curls and waves styled in each area
The tools switched off, unplugged and cooling, plates cleaned
checklist: Helped choose a heat setting that suits the hair and recorded why
Made sure the hair was clean, completely dry and protected
Tested the tool on a tissue or towel before use
Flat ironed small sections smoothly with few passes, using the comb chase
Kept the plates away from the scalp and ears
Made even curls or waves and let them cool before combing
Rested hot tools safely and kept cords tidy and away from water
Switched off, unplugged, cooled and cleaned the tools
safety: Check cords and plugs first; do not use a damaged tool
Test every hot tool on a tissue or towel before it touches the hair
Protect the scalp and ears; use lower heat on fine, treated or damaged hair
Rest hot tools only in a holder or on a heat mat; never leave them alone while on
